# @game-studio/end-game-validator

This readme contains an overview of the end game validator module with usage examples. This is not an exhaustive guide on usage but all the main points and caveats are documented here.

## Usage

```ts
import { EndGameValidator } from '@game-studio/end-game-validator';

const endGameValidator: EndGameValidator = new EndGameValidator();

endGameValidator.setLogger(handleValidationError);

function handleValidationError(message: string): void {
    //handle errors here
    //send message as log or show toast
}
```

also upon receiving begin / continue request call `endGameValidater.startGame` and `endGameValidator.continueGame`

on finishing a game call `endGameValidator.endGame`

to add validation for custom elements implement `IValidator` and add it to the validator using `addItemToValidate`

its worth calling `reset` on start game as going to lobby and restart game, an existing game could still be believed to be in progress and old validators will still be attached

## Development

### Testing

```
npm run test
```
```
npm run test:continuous
```

Testing is ran using Karma and will execute all `**/*.spec.ts` files within the `tests` folder.

The `:continuous` flag is useful while developing because it will watch for changes in the source code and tests and execute the suite accordingly.

#### Coverage

Test coverage is generated and available under `reports/coverage` once a test run has completed.

### Linting

```
npm run lint
```

Runs `eslint` and outputs any errors.

### Building and Documentation

```
npm run build
```

This will clean the distribution folder, build the project and generate the documentation.

### Publishing

This package should not be published manually. Publishing is handled by the parent [game-studio](https://github.com/tombolaltd/game-studio) using lerna.

**Note:** it's worth noting that the private registry the package is published to is defined in the `package.json` file.

### TypeScript

#### tsconfig.json

This package is built in TypeScript and the options are controlled by `tsconfig.json` for use in the IDE.
